name: CROATIA
lead: Croatia hugs the Adriatic Sea. It has over 1,700 km of coastline and more than 1,000 islands. Walled cities look like fairy tales. Waterfalls spill into turquoise pools in its national parks. It is about the size of West Virginia.
geo: Croatia is shaped like a crescent. A thin coastal strip called Dalmatia faces the Adriatic Sea. Summers are hot and dry. The air smells of pine and salt.
Inland there are limestone mountains and green valleys. Plitvice Lakes has 16 turquoise lakes stacked like a staircase, linked by mossy waterfalls.
animals: About 1,000 brown bears roam the forests of Velebit. They are Croatia's largest wild animals. Griffon vultures with 2.5 m wingspans soar above the island of Cres.
The clean Adriatic shelters the short-snouted seahorse. Loggerhead sea turtles nest on quiet beaches each summer. Dolphins often leap beside island ferries.
culture: Croatians invented the necktie. The word 'cravat' comes from 'Croat'. In the 1600s soldiers wore knotted scarves. Zagreb even has a small Cravat Museum!
Klapa is unaccompanied male singing from Dalmatia. UNESCO lists it. It sounds like the sea singing. Croatians also introduced the mechanical pencil.
history: Emperor Diocletian built his retirement palace in Split around AD 295–305. People still live inside its walls. Croatia became a medieval kingdom in 925.
Croatia lived under Hungarian, Ottoman and Habsburg rule, then joined Yugoslavia. It declared independence in 1991 and joined the European Union in 2013.
wows: Croatia has over 1,000 islands, but only about 50 are lived on all year.
Dubrovnik's ancient walls played King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
People live inside a 1,700-year-old Roman palace in Split.
Croatia's red chequered shield is called the šahovnica.
Zagreb's Cravat Museum honours the Croatian necktie.
Plitvice's waterfalls grow about a centimetre each year.
Croatia joined the eurozone in January 2023.

myths.myth: Dalmatian puppies are born with spots
myths.fact: They are born pure white. Spots show up after a few weeks. The breed is named after Dalmatia, in Croatia.

myths.myth: Nikola Tesla was born in America
myths.fact: Tesla was born in 1856 in Smiljan, in today's Croatia. He moved to the USA at age 28.
